role: Admin and governance surface. Owns admin UI and admin API for roles, groups, bindings, reviews, and audit visibility.
stableFocus: Never enforce authorization locally. Always call the engine.
Surface explainability and audit trails clearly to operators.
Every privileged action must produce an audit event via the engine APIs.
Treat the engine's decision contract as immutable from this side.
ownedSurfaces: admin API endpoints that orchestrate engine APIs
governance workflows: approvals, access reviews, separation of duties
operator tooling for audit visibility and policy debugging
doNotTouch: Direct database access to engine tables
boundaryRules: All authorization decisions must go through the engine's decision API.
All mutations to roles, groups, and bindings must go through the engine's control plane APIs.
Never cache decisions on this side beyond a single request scope.
validationDefaults: Run typed contract checks against engine APIs.
Run e2e governance flow tests for approvals and reviews when those flows exist.
Run frontend tests for capability-aware navigation once the admin UI is implemented.
Prefer thin-proxy route tests and typed error passthrough checks until richer admin surfaces land.

workingState.activeArea: Admin is currently a thin API scaffold over engine control-plane and access-review APIs. The next admin work should prioritize governance UX, approval workflows, audit visibility, and operator-facing policy debugging rather than local policy logic.
notes: Stack direction: Next.js or similar React framework + typed engine client from SDK.
Current admin implementation is intentionally thin and must stay engine-faithful. Do not overstate the presence of a full governance surface or UI where only proxy APIs exist.
